Round to nearest even

You will learn

How a GF-T16 add aligns exponents, keeps guard and sticky bits, and rounds the half-way case to even.

Two GF-T16 magnitudes, packed as offset(7) : mant(9), add as significands 512 + mant aligned by their offset difference d. gft_add_rne.t27 caps the shift at 11, because a smaller operand beyond that cannot reach the round bit; it keeps the shifted-out bits as guard and sticky, and rounds to nearest even: up on more than half, and on an exact half only when the quotient is odd, so the result stays even. The spec's one test, add_ones, is the carry case: 1.0 + 1.0 crosses 1024, renormalises to offset 41 and returns 20992, exactly 2.0. Its header says what the silicon version does not: the RTL truncates the aligned operand with a shift, while this spec keeps the guard and sticky, so it is the more accurate of the two, bit-exact to the reference oracle.

Try it

Find the line in gft_add_rne.t27 that caps the alignment shift at 11 and say why. Then decode 20480 and 20992 with value = (1 + mant / 512) * 2^(offset - 40) and check the test add_ones against your own addition.

specs/ternary/gft_add_rne.t27

module GftAddRne;
// #1764 + GF-T: a spec-first GF-T16 same-sign ADD with ROUND-TO-NEAREST-EVEN,
// bit-exact to the ideal oracle (trinity-fpga/conformance/gft16_ref.py). Companion
// to gft_mul_rne.t27: where the silicon gft_add TRUNCATES the aligned operand
// (`>> d`), this keeps the shifted-out bits as guard/sticky and rounds to nearest
// even -- so a spec-first GF-T adder MORE ACCURATE than the silicon RTL.
//
// GF-T16 packed magnitude: [ offset(7) : mant(9) ], value = (1+mant/512)*2^(offset-40).

fn on_comb(a: u16, b: u16) -> u16 {
    var a_off : i32 = (a >> 9) as i32;
    var a_mant : i32 = (a & 511) as i32;
    var b_off : i32 = (b >> 9) as i32;
    var b_mant : i32 = (b & 511) as i32;
    // order so hi has the larger (or equal) exponent offset.
    var hi_off : i32 = b_off;
    var hi_m : i32 = b_mant;
    var lo_off : i32 = a_off;
    var lo_m : i32 = a_mant;
    if (a_off >= b_off) {
        hi_off = a_off; hi_m = a_mant; lo_off = b_off; lo_m = b_mant;
    }
    var hi_sig : i32 = 512 + hi_m;
    var lo_sig : i32 = 512 + lo_m;
    // align the smaller significand right by d; d>=11 contributes nothing to the
    // round bit (lo_sig < 1024 < 2^(d-1)), so cap d at 11 to keep 1<<d in range.
    var d : i32 = hi_off - lo_off;
    if (d > 11) { d = 11; }
    var lo_shift : i32 = lo_sig >> d;
    var lo_rem : i32 = lo_sig - (lo_shift << d);          // shifted-out (fractional) bits
    var sum_int : i32 = hi_sig + lo_shift;                // integer significand sum, [512, 2047]

    var out_off : i32 = hi_off;
    var mant : i32 = 0;
    if (sum_int >= 1024) {
        // renormalize by one bit: guard = sum_int&1, sticky = (lo_rem != 0).
        var g : i32 = sum_int & 1;
        var pre : i32 = sum_int >> 1;                     // new significand [512, 1023]
        mant = pre - 512;
        // round-half-to-even at the shifted-out bit g (with sticky lo_rem).
        if (g == 1) {
            if (lo_rem > 0) { mant = mant + 1; }
            else { if ((pre & 1) == 1) { mant = mant + 1; } }
        }
        out_off = hi_off + 1;
        if (out_off >= 80) { out_off = 80; }
    } else {
        // no renorm: round based on the fractional part lo_rem / 2^d vs 1/2.
        mant = sum_int - 512;
        var twice : i32 = lo_rem << 1;
        var half : i32 = 1 << d;
        if (twice > half) { mant = mant + 1; }
        else { if (twice == half) { if ((sum_int & 1) == 1) { mant = mant + 1; } } }
    }
    // mantissa carry after rounding.
    if (mant >= 512) {
        mant = 0;
        out_off = out_off + 1;
        if (out_off >= 80) { out_off = 80; }
    }
    return ((out_off << 9) | mant) as u16;
}

// 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0 -> offset 41, mant 0 = 20992.
test add_ones { assert_eq(on_comb(20480, 20480), 20992); }
endmodule
